tier.note: Three large prospective pregnancy registries (n > 5,600 monotherapy exposures) report 2.0%–2.9% major congenital malformation rates comparable to the general population; requires pregnancy/postpartum dose monitoring.

refs.quote: Data from several prospective pregnancy exposure registries and epidemiological studies of pregnant women have not detected an increased frequency of major congenital malformations or a consistent pattern of malformations among women exposed to lamotrigine compared with the general population (see Data) .

Women with epilepsy who become pregnant should not abruptly discontinue antiepileptic drugs, including LAMICTAL XR, due to the risk of status epilepticus or severe seizures, which may be life-threatening

The International Lamotrigine Pregnancy Registry reported major congenital malformations in 2.2% (95% CI: 1.6%, 3.1%) of 1,558 infants exposed to lamotrigine monotherapy in the first trimester of pregnancy.

folic_acid.value: Lamotrigine inhibits dihydrofolate reductase in vitro and decreased fetal, placental, and maternal folate concentrations in pregnant rats; reduced folate is associated with teratogenesis.

refs.quote: When oral daily doses of lamotrigine were given to pregnant rats during organogenesis, fetal, placental, and maternal folate concentrations were reduced. Significantly reduced concentrations of folate are associated with teratogenesis

pregnancy_pk.value: Physiological changes during pregnancy may decrease lamotrigine concentrations and/or therapeutic effect; dose adjustments may be necessary to maintain clinical response.

refs.quote: As with other AEDs, physiological changes during pregnancy may affect lamotrigine concentrations and/or therapeutic effect. There have been reports of decreased lamotrigine concentrations during pregnancy and restoration of pre-pregnancy concentrations after delivery. Dose adjustments may be necessary to maintain clinical response.

postpartum.value: Pre-pregnancy lamotrigine concentrations are restored after delivery; maternal serum and milk levels can rise to high levels postpartum if dosage was increased during pregnancy and is not reduced after delivery.

refs.quote: Neonates and young infants are at risk for high serum levels because maternal serum and milk levels can rise to high levels postpartum if lamotrigine dosage has been increased during pregnancy but is not reduced after delivery to the pre-pregnancy dosage.

contraception.value: Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives decrease lamotrigine concentrations by approximately 50%; dosage adjustments are necessary when starting or stopping them, and plasma levels can double during the pill-free week.

refs.quote: Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives decrease lamotrigine concentrations by approximately 50%.
During the week of inactive hormone preparation (pill-free week) of oral contraceptive therapy, plasma lamotrigine levels are expected to rise, as much as doubling at the end of the week.

lactation_summary.value: Present in human milk with infant plasma levels up to 50% of maternal concentrations; monitor breastfed infants closely for rash, apnea, drowsiness, poor sucking, and poor weight gain, and discontinue if toxicity occurs.

refs.quote: Events including rash, apnea, drowsiness, poor sucking, and poor weight gain (requiring hospitalization in some cases) have been reported in infants who have been human milk-fed by mothers using lamotrigine; whether or not these events were caused by lamotrigine is unknown.
Data from multiple small studies indicate that lamotrigine plasma levels in nursing infants have been reported to be as high as 50% of maternal plasma concentrations.
